cells.tense: You are here at the beginning of something and you are not rushing it — the door is open before you know what is walking through.
cells.ask: Offer to stay a moment longer with something that is only beginning, and get back the depth you would have skipped.
cells.core: You can see the whole shape of a situation and still let yourself feel your way into the parts of it you haven't figured out yet. That is rare. Most people either know too soon or feel too late, and you are doing neither. The pieces are still fitting together and you are letting them, which is why what you find holds.\n\nThe invitation here is not to try to understand more — it is to stay one more minute with a thing that hasn't finished showing you what it is. What you receive from that is a knowing that keeps opening instead of one that closes.
cells.sheetLine: You see the whole thing and you let yourself feel your way into it, and it is working.
cells.verb: Opening to feeling before you know what you are feeling
cells.place: Where the whole of a thing comes into view at once

cells.tense: You are already living in an outcome that hasn't happened, bracing for a feeling that isn't here yet.
cells.ask: Choose one thing today from what is actually in front of you and finish it — get back your footing in the present.
cells.core: You can see how a thing fits together and it is a gift. But right now you are seeing the ending before it has arrived, and that seeing has stopped being sight. You are preparing for a feeling nobody has handed you yet. The pattern is real and your reading of it is probably accurate — that is not the problem. The problem is you have stopped receiving and started directing. Everything is being shaped toward a finish line you drew before the race began.\n\nWhat you can do instead is pick one real thing — something small and already underway — and finish it today, by choice. Not the big outcome. The next piece. That is how you come back from ahead of yourself to here.
cells.sheetLine: You are living ahead of where you actually are, and the future isn't yours to write in yet.
cells.verb: Opening to feeling before you know what you are feeling
cells.place: Where the whole of a thing comes into view at once

cells.tense: You are standing at a threshold that is already behind you — the door opened and you kept walking past it.
cells.ask: Show up to one thing today with no preparation and let yourself be new at it — get back the freshness of a first time.
cells.core: You can see the whole pattern when you are in it, and that capacity is not gone. But you have stopped showing up where the pattern is still forming. The way you have been moving has kept you from being caught off guard — and it has kept you from being inside anything. What is missing is the ability to be moved by something you didn't see coming.\n\nYou cannot force feeling into the place that has gone quiet. What you can do is bring yourself to something as if for the first time — unprepared, unpatterned, available. Walk into one thing today without knowing how it goes. That is what returns the openness you have been standing outside of.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped letting yourself be moved by anything, and you are still standing outside the room.
cells.verb: Opening to feeling before you know what you are feeling
cells.place: Where the whole of a thing comes into view at once

cells.tense: You are already open and already receiving, and you are telling yourself you are just being practical.
cells.ask: Name one thing you have felt today and call it feeling, out loud — get back the ownership of your own knowing.
cells.core: You are the one who sees the whole thing and feels it at the same time — that is already running, right now, shaping how you move through this. But it gets described as though it were happening to you rather than through you. You call it being sensible. You call it not getting emotional. Meanwhile the feeling is doing the work and getting called weather.\n\nThe capacity here is not something to build. It is something to claim. Name one feeling you have had today — just for yourself, just once — as yours. That is what returns the thing to the one it belongs to.
cells.sheetLine: You are already feeling your way through this. You just haven't called it yours.
